events.title: Death of Ferdinand Magellan
events.description: Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan was killed in the Battle of Mactan in the Philippines while fighting against the forces of the local chieftain Lapulapu, during the Spanish expedition to circumnavigate the globe.
events.significance: Although Magellan died, the expedition under Juan Sebastián Elcano continued and completed the first circumnavigation of the Earth in 1522, proving the world could be sailed around.

events.title: Sinking of the steamboat Sultana
events.description: The steamboat Sultana exploded and sank on the Mississippi River near Memphis, Tennessee, killing an estimated 1,168 people, most of them Union soldiers recently released from Confederate prison camps.
events.significance: It remains the deadliest maritime disaster in United States history, surpassing the loss of life on the Titanic, though it received limited press coverage because of the end of the Civil War and Lincoln's assassination.

events.title: German forces enter Athens
events.description: During World War II, German troops entered Athens and raised the Nazi swastika flag over the Acropolis, completing the conquest of mainland Greece.
events.significance: The fall of Athens began the Axis occupation of Greece, which brought severe famine and hardship and fueled a strong Greek resistance movement.

events.title: South Africa holds its first multiracial democratic elections
events.description: Millions of South Africans of all races voted in the country's first democratic general election, with voting beginning on April 27, which is now celebrated as Freedom Day.
events.significance: The election marked the end of apartheid and led to Nelson Mandela becoming the country's first Black president, transforming South Africa into a multiracial democracy.

events.title: Birth of Ulysses S. Grant
events.description: Ulysses S. Grant, future commanding general of the Union Army and 18th President of the United States, was born in Point Pleasant, Ohio.
events.significance: Grant led the Union to victory in the American Civil War and, as president, supported Reconstruction and enforcement of civil rights for formerly enslaved people.
